# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 84 (Bu-Vb Pc84)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc84
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 84
**Title (English, from literature):** Picking up precious things

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ratana-sikkhāpada* ("Rule on Precious Things"), designated as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 84, sets out the disciplinary infraction incurred when a Buddhist monk picks up or takes possession of valuable objects (*ratana*) [SuttaCentral]. In modern Vinaya legal analysis, it is highlighted as an example of an offense of omission (*sacittaka*/*acittaka* āpatti), whereby a monastic who finds valuables left behind by a layperson in a monastic dwelling or hall (*kuṭī*, *sālā*) is required to take custody of them for the owner [Vajirañāṇavarorasa]. The rule distinguishes between a monastic residential area (*ārāma*) and a public lodging or hostel (*āvasatha*) when regulating the custody and handling of such items [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is preserved throughout canonical Vinaya literature, appearing in the Theravāda Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 161), both monastic Parivāras, and the corresponding Pācittiya sections of the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda recensions in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus registers extensive Pali-internal text reuse (over 1,000 matches across 137 texts), most prominently with Khandhaka chapters concerning monastic requisites—including the Bhesajjakkhandhaka (Kd 6), Cīvarakkhandhaka (Kd 8), Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1), and Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka (Kd 15)—as well as sibling Vibhaṅga rules such as Pācittiya 85 and Pācittiya 57 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus include Tibetan Prātimokṣa commentaries such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), and the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus].
